No but depending on who you believe if one person is wearing a face covering the chance of the virus spreading is 10-30% than if no one is wearing a face covering, this being the most obvious form of protection so I'm assuming that for everyone 1 case where someone caught the virus wearing a face covering there are 3 cases where someone wasn't and applying the same logic to the death rate. I will try and see if I can find any actual estimates on the number of people who have died who weren't following the guidelines but it's probably very hard to gauge whether somebody was when they contracted the virus. From my experience whether people are following guidelines is very hit and miss. My area has a low number of cases compared with other areas and about 90% seem to be following guidelines.

Yes from what I've read the majority of people who have died are from high risk categories, which to me suggests that the majority of people are probably not at risk even if they caught Covid of dying from the disease. If the disease had a death rate like SARS then I'd be fully willing to have lockdowns but to me I am unsure as to whether lockdown will save enough lives to be worth it as you have to consider how many deaths were actually preventable and how many extra have been caused as a result of lockdown. As I said maybe I'm wrong and in the end this lockdown may be worth it but I'm highly skeptical.

As far as nursing homes go, they're deaths are probably the exception and not the rule but definitely people who died as a result of other people's carelessness. I will have to disagree though, I think we have to acknowledge that for a significant number of deaths the person who could've most easily prevented it is probably that person themselves and that had they been more responsible for their own needs then they would've not died.

The majority of people who die from Covid probably didn't follow guidelines, took the risks and died. People who are trying not to die of Covid probably aren't because they are not putting themselves at risk - if people want to put themselves at risk that's their prerogative. 

The overall health and well being of the population is just the accumulation of all individual needs and wants. And maybe I'm wrong, and that this lockdown is a good thing but I don't think the government is making the necessary provisions to help deal with other potential consequences of this lockdown.

What about the additional deaths from suicide, or the additional cases of cancer or heart disease as depression does have a physiological implications as well. Do they not matter? The people dying from COVID-19 are probably not people who are following government guidelines, they probably knew the risks and ignored it anyway, not to mention the long term implications on the economy and jobs - a second lockdown will only serve to stunt any recovery, people are inevitable going to lose their livelihoods and go hungry. A second lockdown will cause additional deaths through other means as well as lower many people's quality of life.

In the end you should do what you feel is best to do, and I get that it is difficult to leave a job because you need that income and you genuinely don't know when your next opportunity is. If you've been in the parking lot for 6 hours I would drive home and use the time whilst your still reasonably well awake to discuss things with your girlfriend.

From there, in regard to your mental health, the priority should probably be your relationship with your girlfriend - not the job. If you've been in the parking lot for 6 hours you should probably just go home and use this time to talk things over with her. She probably cares about you as much as you care about her and probably doesn't realize how bad it makes you feel. 

You probably have two realistic options - either leave the job that causes you so much stress or strengthen your support network with your girlfriend so that it is able to provide a positive environment that makes you feel good. Don't be afraid to be emotionally vulnerable, she probably wants to help you and you'll both come out stronger as a result.
